LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Weather and Our Environment Suggested Vocabulary: sun, shine, rain, clouds, blow
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Weather and Our Environment Suggested Vocabulary: sun, shine, rain, clouds, blow in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we show we are listening when someone is talking to us?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

B. identify words featuring the sounds /f/, /n/ /h/ / ɒ/ and / ɔː/ from an oral text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. pronounce words with the sounds /f/, /n/ /h/ / ɒ/ and / ɔː/ for oral fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. responding to simple specific one- directional instructions using new words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the need for correct pronunciation in communication. • Learners to listen to an audio text containing the target sounds: /f/, /n/ /h/ / ɒ/ and / ɔː/ and identify words with the target sounds. • Learners are guided to individually to say the target sounds as modelled by peers/ teacher / audio recording. • Learners use a Frayer model to discuss the meaning of words with the target sounds in sentences. • Learners to recite rhymes/sing songs about weather. • Learners to listen to a story related the theme and discuss the story using the new words. • Learners are guided to role play How do we show we are listening when someone is talking to us? 53 responding to simple instructions related to the theme, using appropriate eye contact and facial expressions. Learners with blindness are given one on one demonstration of various facial expressions and clear verbal descriptions.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration -The learner’s listening skills are enhanced as the learner listens and responds to simple instructions in a role play.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as the learner displays team spirit in group and pair activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion is enhanced as the learners work collaboratively in group or pair activities

Link to other learning areas

Attentive listening is emphasised in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language activities.

Suggested learning resources

• Braille letter cards,

• Audio, video clip,

• Textbooks in braille and in appropriate font and colour contrast.
